question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(2),$ calculate $P(X>6\,|\,X>4).$
question.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the momeryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =2,$ $s=4,$ and $s+t=6.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=6-4=2
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6\,|\,X>4) & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(2)\cdot (2)} \\  & ={e}^{-4} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
